topic: Using Standard Template Library (STL) Containers Correctly
explanation: The Standard Template Library (STL) provides powerful containers like `vector`, `map`, and `set`.  Understanding how to correctly construct and use these containers is crucial for writing efficient and idiomatic C++ code. A common pitfall is attempting to initialize containers with incompatible types, leading to compilation errors.  For example, directly initializing a `vector<string>` with a single string literal will fail because the constructor expects an initializer list or a size and optional value. Best practices involve using initializer lists for initialization or employing range-based for loops for adding elements iteratively.
